title: Attribution ledger entry -- claim / actor / verified-by / timestamp
description: v2 (2026-08-25, Pavlo's mechanical-not-prose-only round): adds entry_id (deterministic, content-addressed -- same pattern this repo already uses for decision_ref/artifact_hash, see services/proof_signing.py::sign_payload) and a structured surface classification, replacing v1's free-text surface string. Generalizes Damon's own v0.3.x companion doc §13 pattern into a machine-checkable format. Entries are only trustworthy once independently reproduced -- an entry with no verified_by is a self-assertion, not a ledger row.

entry_id.description: Deterministic, content-addressed identity -- 'sha256:' + hex(sha256(canonical_bytes)), where canonical_bytes is the RFC 8785 JCS encoding of every OTHER field in this object (claim, actor, verified_by, timestamp, surface, type, evidence), sorted keys, entry_id itself excluded from the preimage to avoid circularity. Same construction this repo already uses for decision_ref/artifact_hash (services/proof_signing.py::sign_payload) -- reused rather than invented, per Pavlo's ask that edges reference an exact identity rather than a free-form id/commit/hash string. Two independently-authored entries with byte-identical content necessarily share an entry_id; that's intentional, not a collision bug -- it means the same claim was recorded twice, which is itself useful signal, not an error to prevent.

claim.description: What was found, proved, audited, verified, or built -- in enough detail that a stranger reading only this field understands the unit of work without following a link. Not a summary of a conversation; a statement of the specific contribution.

actor.description: Who did the work this entry claims. A stable handle (GitHub username, group-known name), not a display name that can drift. The person credited here did NOT necessarily type a commit -- see `type`.

oneOf.description: Name only -- v1-compatible, acceptable when no separate verification artifact exists yet.

evidence_ref.description: A URL, commit, or recompute reference for THIS verifier's own confirmation -- distinct from the claim's own `evidence` field, which documents the original claim, not the act of verifying it.

oneOf.description: Preferred form once a real verification artifact exists (Pavlo's ask: 'verification should eventually resolve to evidence-bearing verification refs, not only names'). Both forms are valid in v2 -- the bare-string form is not deprecated, since not every real verification produces its own separate citable artifact (e.g. a reviewer confirming a claim by reading code directly, with the confirmation itself only recorded as this ledger row).

verified_by.description: Who independently reproduced or confirmed the claim -- REQUIRED, non-empty. This is the field that makes an entry a ledger row rather than a self-assertion. An actor cannot be the sole verified_by for their own claim -- at least one entry in this array must name someone other than `actor`.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 UTC, an actual event timestamp (Pavlo's ask, v2: tighten examples to real times, not round/approximate ones). When the claim was made, not when it was verified.

classification.description: Closed enum (Pavlo's ask, v2) so vertice_product/commons/vendor/external can never be conflated by inference. `commons`: a trustless-ai-owned or group-owned surface (e.g. this ledger's own format, agent-ercs, recompute-kit). `vertice_product`: a Vertice-owned product surface (e.g. AgentMarketEscrow). `vendor`: a third-party vendor/build relationship's own surface (e.g. invinoveritas's own repo/product, when the entry is about invinoveritas's own work rather than something done ON a Vertice or commons surface). `external`: any other party's surface entirely (e.g. crewAI, w3c-cg -- real interop work that isn't owned by anyone in this ledger's own group).

identifier.description: The specific repo/product/artifact within that classification -- e.g. 'trustless-ai/recompute-kit', 'vertice/agentmarketescrow', 'invinoveritas', 'crewAIInc/crewAI#4877'.

surface.description: Structured, never free text (v2) -- this is the field a value-sharing formula reads to answer 'was this verified work done ON this specific Vertice surface,' and a free-text string left that answerable only by inference, which is exactly the conflation risk Pavlo flagged.

type.description: The five contribution types named explicitly in damon:general 2026-08-25 (Pavlo/Merlini), each first-class regardless of whether it produced a commit. 'find' = discovered a gap/bug/defect. 'prove' = constructed a demonstration or proof the claim holds. 'audit' = reviewed existing work against a spec/claim. 'verify' = independently reproduced someone else's result. 'build' = implemented/shipped the artifact itself (the only type that typically has a `commit` field).

evidence.description: What makes this entry independently reproducible rather than asserted. At least one of the fields below MUST be present; which one depends on the entry's type.

commit.description: Full immutable commit SHA -- mechanically constrained to exactly 40 hex chars (v2.1, Pavlo's ask: constrain, don't just describe), when the contribution has one. Absent for pure discovery/audit/verification work that never touched a diff -- absence here is NOT a gap, it's the exact case this ledger exists to make first-class.

url.description: A PR, issue comment, or published artifact URL a third party can open and check directly.

recompute.description: A stated procedure (or reference to one) that lets a stranger reproduce the claim independently -- e.g. 'recompute sha256 over the JCS-canonicalized preimage, compare to the published digest'.

hash.description: A content hash the claim can be checked against, when applicable (e.g. a vectors file's own sha256).

accessibility.description: Explicit classification of whether a stranger can actually open/check the evidence CARRIER above -- a URL behind a private group's access, or a reference to a conversation with no public record, is real evidence but not equally checkable by everyone. `accessibility` describes a carrier; it is never itself a carrier -- see the object-level `anyOf` below, added v2.1 after Pavlo flagged that `minProperties: 1` let `{"accessibility": ...}` alone satisfy the requirement with no actual evidence present.

notes.description: Optional. Context that doesn't belong in `claim` itself -- e.g. a correction to an earlier entry, a caveat on scope. EXCLUDED from the entry_id preimage (v2.1, resolving an ambiguity Pavlo flagged: `notes` is commentary ABOUT an already-identified entry, so it must be free to add or edit -- e.g. appending a correction -- without changing the entry's own content-addressed identity. entry_id's preimage is exactly {claim, actor, verified_by, timestamp, surface, type, evidence}, the seven REQUIRED fields, nothing optional included.
